explanation:
I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is about the library's own definition `spaceGrad` (from `AVenhance/Statements/Roots/SpaceGrad.lean`), defined as `fun x i => fderiv ℝ f x (basisVec i)`. It says that this gradient of a finite sum is the sum of the gradients.

Mathlib has nothing about `spaceGrad`. The only Mathlib ingredient is `fderiv_sum`, which says the Fréchet derivative is additive. That is a generic linearity law, like `map_add`, being applied to a library definition, so the mathematical content lies in the library's definition. The current proof also does more than apply one lemma. It uses `funext`, rewrites the function as a finite sum, applies `fderiv_sum`, and then unfolds `spaceGrad` and evaluates the sum of continuous linear maps. That is more than a one- or two-line instantiation of a single Mathlib result. I checked the definition of `spaceGrad` and found no gradient-of-sum lemma in Mathlib that applies to this custom basis-vector gradient.
